epic.title: Testing Infrastructure
epic.description: Shared testing harnesses, runners, fixture infrastructure, and CI wiring for the MTC CA per spec section 19: proptest conventions, four-layer fuzzing (19.3), conformance and differential runners against the bwesterb/mtc Go reference, fault-injection backends powering the adversarial (19.8) and chaos (19.9) suites, soak/perf/cross-version harnesses, Kani/Loom/Shuttle CI integration (19.12, 22.13), and the E2E-via-CLI harness (19.13). Component-specific tests ship with their component epics; this epic owns everything those tests plug into, all runnable on a laptop against LocalStack/SoftHSM/memory backends per section 1 non-goals (no cloud spend).

tickets.title: Shared test-support crate with fixtures and proptest conventions
tickets.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/mtc-testutil`: shared fixture builders, deterministic RNG/temp-dir helpers, and the proptest conventions layer required by spec 19.2 and 19.3 Layer 1, so component epics write property tests against one common toolkit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New dev-dependency crate `crates/mtc-testutil` with seeded-RNG helper, temp-dir/env helpers, and fixture builders for checkpoints, log entries, and tree-leaf sequences (built on core-mtc-types)
- Shared proptest strategy helpers and a documented `Arbitrary` convention (impls live with each spec type behind a `testing` feature flag)
- CI wiring runs proptest with extended iterations for spec types (PROPTEST_CASES >= 10,000 per 19.3 Layer 1) while local default stays fast (<30s unit budget per 19.1)
- `proptest-regressions/` seed files checked in; convention documented in crate docs
- One exemplar property test (round-trip on a core type) exercising the helpers

## Out of Scope
- Component property tests themselves (ship with component tickets per epic boundary)
- Fuzz targets and corpus (test-fuzz-harness)
- Fault-injection wrappers (test-fault-injection)

## Testing
- Unit tests for helpers; exemplar property test per 19.2

## Demo
`cargo test -p mtc-testutil`, then `PROPTEST_CASES=10000 cargo test` showing extended-iteration mode.

tickets.title: Spec conformance suite runner and test-vector infrastructure
tickets.description:
## Goal
Build the clean-room spec conformance suite (spec 19.4, roadmap Phase 1): a test-vector format plus a runner that serves as an ongoing CI gate for MTC wire-format and verification behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `conformance/vectors/` directory with a documented JSON+hex fixture format for spec structures (checkpoints, proofs, entries) and a README describing how to add vectors
- Runner discovers every vector and asserts parse/serialize/verify expectations, including must-reject vectors with expected error class
- Failure output identifies vector ID and shows a structural diff, not just an assertion failure
- Suite runs on every PR under `cargo test --all-features` (required check per 22.13)
- Seeded with clean-room vectors: checkpoint and inclusion-proof happy paths plus at least 3 invalid cases

## Out of Scope
- Cross-language differential comparison (test-differential-runner)
- Vectors for structures not yet implemented (added by component tickets)

## Testing
- Unit tests for the vector loader; the suite itself is the conformance layer (19.4)

## Demo
`make conformance` prints per-vector pass/fail and total counts.

tickets.title: Go reference shim wrapping bwesterb/mtc for cross-language testing
tickets.description:
## Goal
Provide a small Go CLI shim around `bwesterb/mtc` exposing parse/verify subcommands, the invocation helper on the Rust side, and the CI build step — the foundation for differential testing per spec 19.3 Layer 4 and 19.5 (refer to the Go code, never copy it, per roadmap Phase 1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `tools/mtc-go-shim/` Go module with subcommands `parse-checkpoint`, `parse-proof`, `verify-inclusion`: bytes on stdin, canonical JSON on stdout, nonzero exit plus machine-readable error on reject
- `bwesterb/mtc` version pinned in go.mod; `make go-shim` builds locally
- CI job builds and caches the shim binary for downstream jobs
- Rust wrapper in mtc-testutil spawns the shim with a timeout and typed result (the `call_go_binary` seam from 19.3 Layer 4)
- Ships as 2 PRs: (1) Go shim + CI build/cache, (2) Rust invocation wrapper

## Out of Scope
- The differential runner and mismatch handling (test-differential-runner)
- Nightly job wiring (test-differential-runner)

## Testing
- Unit test for the Rust wrapper; integration test round-tripping one known vector through the shim

## Demo
`make go-shim && echo <hex-vector> | tools/mtc-go-shim/bin/shim parse-checkpoint` emits parsed JSON.

tickets.title: Differential test runner (Rust vs Go reference) with nightly CI job
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement the differential runner comparing our parser/verifier against the Go reference shim (spec 19.3 Layer 4, 19.5): agreement on accept, agreement on reject, structural equality of parsed forms — run nightly in CI due to cross-language tooling cost.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Runner semantics per 19.3 Layer 4: both accept -> assert structural equality (canonical JSON compare); both reject -> pass; disagreement -> fail with the offending input persisted
- Input sources: conformance vectors, proptest-generated cases, and `fuzz/corpus/` entries when present
- Dual-path verification hook per 19.5: verify the same proof via our logic and via the shim, fail on disagreement
- Nightly scheduled CI job with mismatch inputs uploaded as artifacts; `make differential INPUT=<file>` reproduces locally

## Out of Scope
- Building the Go shim (test-go-ref-shim)
- Per-issuance differential checks inside the CA service (component epics reuse this runner)

## Testing
- Unit tests for the comparator; the suite itself is the differential layer (19.5)

## Demo
`make differential` runs the full corpus locally against the built shim and prints agree/disagree counts.

tickets.title: cargo-fuzz scaffolding, corpus management, and CI wiring
tickets.description:
## Goal
Stand up the unstructured fuzzing layer (spec 19.3 Layer 2) and its corpus-management workflow: `fuzz/` workspace, checked-in corpora, crash-to-regression promotion, and CI jobs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- cargo-fuzz `fuzz/` setup with one exemplar target `parse_checkpoint` asserting no panic on arbitrary bytes, plus a documented template for the one-target-per-parseable-type convention (Checkpoint, MTCProof, RevocationList, TBSCertificateLogEntry, Tile, ACME body — remaining targets ship with component epics)
- `fuzz/corpus/<target>/` checked into the repo, seeded with hand-crafted seeds plus conformance vectors once available (19.3 corpus management)
- Documented promotion workflow: minimized crash inputs become permanent unit-test regression fixtures
- CI: PR job replays corpus (no exploration) per target; nightly job fuzzes each target for a fixed budget with minimized crash artifacts uploaded
- Allocation/RSS limits and per-input timeout configured so unbounded-allocation and unbounded-depth inputs fail (19.3 asserted properties)

## Out of Scope
- Structured `arbitrary`-bridge targets (test-structured-fuzz)
- Fuzz targets for types owned by other epics

## Testing
- Fuzz (self); unit test proving the exemplar corpus replays clean

## Demo
`cargo +nightly fuzz run parse_checkpoint -- -runs=10000` completes with no crashes.

tickets.title: Structured fuzzing helpers via the arbitrary bridge
tickets.description:
## Goal
Provide the structured-fuzzing layer (spec 19.3 Layer 3): shared `arbitrary`-based generators producing semi-valid structures so fuzzing reaches post-parse verification paths that byte-level fuzzing misses.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `Arbitrary` impls/helpers for structured inputs (e.g., `ArbitraryProofInput`) in mtc-testutil behind a feature flag
- Exemplar structured target per 19.3: construct a proof from arbitrary structured input, run verification, assert no panic
- Structured targets run under the same PR-replay and nightly CI wiring as byte-level targets
- Docs: decision guidance for structured vs unstructured targets, added to the fuzz template README

## Out of Scope
- Structured targets for component-owned types (ship with those epics)
- Byte-level target scaffolding (test-fuzz-harness)

## Testing
- Fuzz (structured, 19.3 Layer 3); unit test for generator validity bounds

## Demo
`cargo +nightly fuzz run verify_proof_structured -- -runs=10000` exercises post-parse verification without panics.

tickets.title: Kani CI integration with critical-path gating
tickets.description:
## Goal
Wire `cargo kani` into CI per spec 19.12 and the 22.13 required-check rule (critical-path PRs must pass proofs), with conventions and a sentinel proof so component epics (tree primitives, lease/epoch, write-path linearization) add harnesses that run unmodified.

## Acceptance Criteria
- CI job installs a pinned Kani release with toolchain caching and runs `cargo kani` across crates opted in via a documented marker
- Path-filter gating per 22.13: the check is required only when critical-path crates change; a nightly job runs all proofs unconditionally
- Sentinel harness in mtc-testutil (`#[cfg(kani)]` module, small provable property with unwind bound) proves the wiring end-to-end and stays green
- Conventions doc: harness placement in `#[cfg(kani)]` modules, naming scheme, unwind-bound annotations, and how to opt a crate in

## Out of Scope
- Real Kani harnesses (core-mtc-library and multi-region epics own their proofs per 19.12)
- Loom/Shuttle wiring (test-loom-shuttle-ci)

## Testing
- Kani (sentinel harness); CI-config validation on a critical-path-touching PR

## Demo
Open a PR touching an opted-in crate: the `cargo kani` check appears and passes; `cargo kani -p mtc-testutil` reproduces locally.

tickets.title: Loom and Shuttle CI integration and authoring conventions
tickets.description:
## Goal
Wire Loom interleaving tests and Shuttle randomized concurrency tests into CI per spec 19.12, ahead of the Phase 5 lease-renewer/batch-builder concurrency tests (roadmap section 24), with sentinel tests proving the wiring.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dedicated CI job runs loom tests with `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom"`; loom tests are excluded from the normal `cargo test` run
- Shuttle job with a fixed iteration budget; failing schedules are persisted with documented reproduction steps
- Sentinel loom test and sentinel shuttle test in mtc-testutil keep both jobs green before component tests land
- Conventions doc: `cfg(loom)` type-swapping pattern (loom::sync vs std::sync), test placement, and when to use Shuttle vs Loom (19.12: Shuttle for properties too expensive to model-check exhaustively)
- Ships as 2 PRs: (1) Loom job + sentinel + doc, (2) Shuttle job + sentinel + doc

## Out of Scope
- The real concurrency tests (multi-region and ca-service epics author them)
- Kani wiring (test-kani-ci)

## Testing
- Loom + Shuttle (sentinel tests); CI-config validation

## Demo
`make loom` runs the interleaving suite locally; CI shows the loom and shuttle jobs green on a PR.

tickets.title: E2E-via-CLI harness, shell helpers, and CI job
tickets.description:
## Goal
Build the `tests/e2e/` harness per spec 19.13 and 19.1: E2E tests are plain shell scripts driving `mtcctl` against the full demo environment — a deliberate agent affordance.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `tests/e2e/` layout with a runner (`make e2e`) that boots the demo environment (LocalStack + SoftHSM per 19.1), discovers `*.sh` tests, runs each hermetically, and prints a pass/fail summary
- Shared shell helper library: assertions, wait-for/retry, JSON extraction via jq
- Rust-authored E2E tests supported alongside shell scripts (19.1)
- First smoke test lands: issue -> lookup -> inclusion verified, matching the 19.13 example verbatim
- CI job runs the E2E suite with service logs uploaded on failure

## Out of Scope
- Additional demo-scenario tests (issue/verify/revoke/prune scripts ship with their feature epics)
- Soak-mode load driving (test-soak-harness)

## Testing
- E2E (19.1, 19.13); unit tests for any Rust runner code

## Demo
`make e2e` on a laptop boots the env and passes the issuance-and-verification smoke test.
deps: EXTERNAL:mtcctl cert issue/lookup and log inclusion commands (admin-surface + ca-service)

tickets.title: Fault-injection wrappers for cloud abstraction backends
tickets.description:
## Goal
Provide decorator backends implementing the cloud traits that inject configurable faults — the shared machinery behind the adversarial suite (spec 19.8), chaos scenarios (19.9), and component-level failure tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `FaultInjecting<T>` wrappers for `ObjectStore`, `ObjectLock`, `ReplicatedKv`, and `Hsm`: error injection, latency injection, replication-stall simulation, and a wrong-signature HSM mode (19.8)
- Faults are scriptable and deterministic: triggered by operation count, key pattern, or explicit toggle; seedable for reproduction
- Test-clock utility supporting forced clock skew for lease-related tests (19.8, 19.9)
- Ships as a dev-dependency consumable by all component epics; wraps the memory backend with zero external dependencies (19.1 unit-test constraint)
- Unit tests cover every injector mode

## Out of Scope
- Scenario definitions built on top (test-chaos-harness, adversarial tickets)
- Process-level fault actions like killing a region (test-chaos-harness)

## Testing
- Unit + property (injector determinism given a seed)

## Demo
`cargo test -p mtc-testutil fault_injection` shows a wrong-signature HSM causing checkpoint verification to fail cleanly.

tickets.title: Chaos scenario harness for the local multi-region simulation
tickets.description:
## Goal
Build the chaos-engineering framework per spec 19.9: named scenarios with machine-checked pass/fail criteria, running fault actions against the local multi-region simulation — no cloud spend per section 1 non-goals.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Scenario abstraction: named scenario = setup + injected fault + pass criterion, mirroring the 19.9 table schema
- Fault action library: kill region process, CRR delay/stall, DDB lag, HSM down, clock skew, entry flood — built on test-fault-injection plus process control of the dev simulation
- Runner: `make chaos SCENARIO=<name>` and `make chaos` (all), emitting machine-readable results per scenario
- First scenario end-to-end: chaos-primary-loss (kill primary mid-batch -> new primary promotes; no committed cert lost)
- Chaos suite wired as a scheduled CI job (not per-PR)

## Out of Scope
- Remaining 19.9 scenarios (test-chaos-epoch-scenarios, test-chaos-infra-scenarios)
- The multi-region simulation environment itself (multi-region epic)

## Testing
- Chaos/integration (19.9); unit tests for the runner and fault actions

## Demo
`make chaos SCENARIO=chaos-primary-loss` kills the primary mid-batch and reports PASS with the promotion evidence.
deps: EXTERNAL:multi-region simulation in dev environment (multi-region epic)

tickets.title: Chaos scenarios: split-brain, old-primary recovery, clock skew
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement the epoch-invariant chaos scenarios from the spec 19.9 table — the scenarios that exercise the core multi-region trust story (roadmap Phase 5 chaos scenarios).

## Acceptance Criteria
- chaos-split-brain: both regions attempt promotion -> exactly one succeeds (epoch invariant asserted)
- chaos-old-primary-recovery: failed primary returns -> automatically stands down to read-only
- chaos-clock-skew: +/-60s skew between regions -> lease semantics remain correct
- Each scenario has an automated pass criterion matching the 19.9 table, is registered in the chaos runner, and runs in the scheduled CI chaos job
- Failures capture region logs and epoch/lease state for debugging

## Out of Scope
- Infrastructure-fault scenarios (test-chaos-infra-scenarios)
- Fixes to lease/epoch bugs these scenarios find (filed against multi-region epic)

## Testing
- Chaos/integration (19.9)

## Demo
`make chaos SCENARIO=chaos-split-brain` shows one promotion succeeding, one rejected, PASS.

tickets.title: Chaos scenarios: CRR stall, DDB lag, HSM down, adapter flood
tickets.description:
## Goal
Complete the full chaos suite (spec 19.9 table; roadmap Phase 8) with the infrastructure-fault scenarios.

## Acceptance Criteria
- chaos-crr-stall: injected 30-min (simulated) CRR delay -> failover waits for catchup
- chaos-ddb-lag: forced replicated-KV lag -> no split-brain; reads are stale, never incorrect
- chaos-hsm-down: HSM unavailable mid-batch -> batch retries, the observability epic's HSM-down alert signal fires, service eventually stands down
- chaos-adapter-flood: adapter floods entries -> backpressure engages; no accepted entries lost
- All registered in the chaos runner and scheduled CI job; each independently runnable via `make chaos SCENARIO=<name>`

## Out of Scope
- Epoch-invariant scenarios (test-chaos-epoch-scenarios)
- Alerting/metric definitions asserted here (observability epic owns them)

## Testing
- Chaos/integration (19.9)

## Demo
`make chaos SCENARIO=chaos-hsm-down` shows retry, alert, and stand-down sequence ending in PASS.

tickets.title: Adversarial suite: wire, proof, and signing attacks
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement the wire/crypto half of the spec 19.8 adversarial suite: automated attacks on parsing, proof generation, and signing invariants, each asserting a specific rejection rather than mere absence of crash.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Malformed tiles fed to inclusion-proof generation -> typed error, no panic, no bogus proof (19.8)
- Wrong signatures from a "compromised" HSM (fault-injection wrong-sig mode) -> checkpoint verification rejects with a signature error
- Replayed old checkpoints -> rejected by freshness/monotonicity checks with the expected error class
- Crafted public keys attempting key-hash collisions -> rejected; hash domain separation asserted
- Malformed-input builders (tiles, keys, checkpoints) land in mtc-testutil for reuse by component epics
- Suite gated behind `--features integration` (19.1), runs under the existing `cargo test --all-features` check (22.13); `make redteam` target added

## Out of Scope
- Coordination-layer attacks (test-adversarial-coordination)
- Fixing vulnerabilities found (filed against owning epics)

## Testing
- Adversarial/integration (19.8); unit tests for input builders

## Demo
`make redteam` shows the replayed-old-checkpoint test rejecting with the expected error.

tickets.title: Adversarial suite: lease, epoch, and allocation attacks
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement the coordination half of the spec 19.8 adversarial suite: attacks on lease/epoch, index allocation, and replication invariants, each asserting the invariant holds or the write is rejected.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Stalled CRR plus attempted promotion -> promotion refused until catchup (19.8)
- Forced clock skew via the test clock (+/-60s) -> lease semantics remain correct
- Duplicate index allocation attempts -> exactly one succeeds; allocated ranges never overlap
- Stale-epoch writes -> rejected by conditional checks with a typed error
- Runs against the memory backend with fault injection: deterministic and seedable, no LocalStack required (19.1)
- Gated behind `--features integration` and included in the `make redteam` target

## Out of Scope
- Wire/crypto attacks (test-adversarial-wire)
- Chaos process-level scenarios (chaos tickets)

## Testing
- Adversarial/integration (19.8); property test for allocation non-overlap under concurrent attack

## Demo
`make redteam` shows the stale-epoch write rejected and the duplicate-allocation attack producing exactly one winner.

tickets.title: Soak test harness with PR and overnight modes
tickets.description:
## Goal
Build the soak harness per spec 19.7: long-running workloads that catch memory leaks, Tokio task leaks, lease starvation, cache eviction issues, and HSM connection-pool exhaustion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Workload driver generating sustained issuance + verification load against the demo environment with configurable rate and duration
- Leak detectors with trend assertions: process RSS, Tokio task count (via the service's runtime-metrics endpoint), open FDs/connections, lease-renewal continuity, cache hit-rate stability
- 10-minute PR mode (19.7) — label-gated to keep PR CI fast — and a scheduled overnight run producing a report artifact
- Failures include time-series of tracked metrics for diagnosis

## Out of Scope
- Latency percentile tracking (test-perf-regression)
- Metric endpoint implementation (observability epic)
- Fixing leaks found (filed against owning epics)

## Testing
- Soak (19.7); unit tests for detectors (synthetic leak triggers detection)

## Demo
`make soak DURATION=10m` runs the short profile locally and prints the leak-check report.
deps: EXTERNAL:service metrics endpoint exposing Tokio runtime/task counts (observability epic)

tickets.title: Cross-version compatibility fixtures and runner
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement spec 19.10: versioned fixtures of historical log states plus a compatibility runner proving current code can always read and extend logs produced by earlier versions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `fixtures/log-states/<version>/` format: serialized log-state snapshot (tiles, checkpoints, entries, metadata) plus a manifest describing producing version and expected invariants
- Capture tool (`make capture-fixture`) snapshots the log state produced by the local demo issuance flow into a new versioned fixture
- Compat runner: for every historical fixture, current code loads it, all checkpoints/proofs still verify, and a fresh append succeeds
- Runs on every PR (fixtures kept small); adding a fixture is documented as part of release/tagging flow
- First fixture captured from the current implementation

## Out of Scope
- Migration tooling for incompatible changes (operational-tooling epic)
- Wire-format versioning design decisions (core-mtc-library)

## Testing
- Integration (fixture load against memory backend); unit tests for manifest parsing

## Demo
`make compat` loads every fixture and prints per-version verification results.

tickets.title: Performance benchmark harness and regression CI gate
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement spec 19.11: benchmarks tracking p50/p99/p99.9 over time with a CI gate that fails on regression beyond threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Benchmark harness (criterion or latency-histogram based) covering key operations: tree append, inclusion-proof generation, proof verification, serialization round-trip; reports p50/p99/p99.9
- Baseline results stored in-repo (JSON) with a deliberate `make bench-baseline` update path reviewed in PRs
- CI job compares current run to baseline with a configurable threshold (e.g., >10% p99 regression fails); warmup and fixed iteration counts documented to control noise
- History retained across runs (artifact or branch) satisfying the "over time" tracking requirement (19.11)

## Out of Scope
- Service-level latency SLOs and dashboards (observability epic)
- Benchmarks for components not yet built (added by their epics using this harness)

## Testing
- Performance (19.11); unit test for the comparator threshold logic

## Demo
`make bench` runs locally and prints percentile table plus delta vs baseline.

tickets.title: Testing guide: layers, commands, and authoring conventions
tickets.description:
## Goal
Write `docs/testing.md`, the authoritative guide to every test layer in spec 19.1-19.13: what each layer is for, the exact command to run it locally, and how to author new tests — including the agent affordance that E2E tests are plain shell (19.13). Part of Phase 8 documentation polish.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Documents each layer with its command: `cargo test`, `cargo test --features integration`, `make e2e`, `make conformance`, `make differential`, fuzz, `cargo kani`, `make loom`, `make chaos`, `make redteam`, `make soak`, `make bench`, `make compat`
- Decision table mapping ticket types to required test layers, matching the 25.4 ticket template's Testing section
- Documents corpus/fixture conventions: `fuzz/corpus/`, `proptest-regressions/`, conformance vectors, versioned log-state fixtures
- Linked from README and AGENTS.md so agents discover it

## Out of Scope
- Runbooks and operational docs (observability/operational epics)
- CI configuration changes

## Testing
- Doc examples validated: every listed command executes successfully on a laptop

## Demo
Open `docs/testing.md`; copy-paste any command block and it runs.
